description: Questions a downstream reasoner might be asked about the LHC micro black hole safety case, authored from corpus/blackholes/posts. Factual, comparative, what-is-the-crux and how-confident-should-I-be forms. The probe asks a reasoner each one with and without the graph's record (#334 S5); diagnostic only.

questions.question: Could a black hole produced at the LHC grow to endanger the Earth?
questions.note: The headline question the cluster settles; the record should carry a near-settled 'no' with high credence.

questions.question: Can the LHC produce microscopic black holes at all, and under what theoretical assumptions?
questions.note: Standard Model says no; extra-dimensional models say yes at ~1/s. Tests whether the conditional scope survives.

questions.question: Has Hawking radiation been directly observed experimentally?
questions.note: The record should say: broad consensus on its reality, no direct experimental evidence. A reasoner conflating consensus with observation is the miss.

questions.question: Which argument for LHC safety is more robust: that micro black holes evaporate via Hawking radiation, or that white dwarfs and neutron stars would already have been destroyed by cosmic-ray-produced black holes?
questions.note: Giddings & Mangano hold the astrophysical bound stands even without Hawking radiation.

questions.question: How does the strangelet risk at the LHC compare with the risk at lower-energy colliders such as RHIC?
questions.note: Strangelet production probability decreases with energy.

questions.question: What is the crux between Plaga's metastable black hole scenario and the Giddings–Mangano safety argument?
questions.note: Whether metastable black holes escape the white-dwarf/neutron-star bounds; G&M say the scenario is internally inconsistent.

questions.question: What is the strongest remaining objection to the claim that the LHC poses no conceivable danger, and has it been answered?
questions.note: Plaga 2008; rebutted by G&M and Casadio et al.; not peer-reviewed.

questions.question: How confident should I be that cosmic-ray collisions have already produced everything the LHC can produce?
questions.note: The load-bearing 'nature has already run the experiment' premise.

questions.question: How confident should I be that a stable microscopic black hole trapped inside the Earth would accrete matter too slowly to matter?
questions.note: The Planck-length accretion argument; the record should hold it as supported/verified.

questions.question: How confident should I be that the LSAG safety review was independent of CERN's institutional interest in running the LHC?
questions.note: Johnson's epistemic objection (specialists are invested). Tests whether the reasoner reaches past the physics claims to the sociology the record may not carry.
